items.title: 52300_Trummy Young oral history interview
items.q: The interviewee discusses Zilner Randolph in the context of arrangers for other bands (Louis Armstrong, Earl Hines, Count Basie/Lunceford) but does not state a personal or professional relationship with Randolph himself.

ctx.x: Oh, several people. Let me see. Some guys not even in the band. Let me see. Jimmy Munday and Cecil Irwin did most of the arranging. The one got killed, the tenor man I told you (Inaudible) -- until he got killed. They did most of the writing, but he had three or four guys -- Joe Massick, he did writing. You probably never knew him. He's from the downtown Loop in Chicago. But he had several people -- writers that
you never heard much about that did a lot of writing too for the band. Zilner Randolph would do somethings.

Zilner used to write for Louis years ago, you know. And he'd do a few things for Earl. It's just like Lunceford's band. Lunceford had quite a few -- Lunceford had quite a few arrangers at -- in that band that -- that wrote for that band and never played with him, you know. People -- one of the best arrangers we had was William -- Billy Moore -- William Moore, Junior. He went to Europe years ago. But he wrote things like "What's your story, Morning Glory" and those things for Lunceford's band.
